- Enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine development by Adimmune (6547-TW) reported durable pediatric immunity, with data presented at ACPID 2026 in Indonesia last week. Long-term immunogenicity shows 6–7 years post-vaccination, antibody levels remain high and serum seroprotection reaches 98.2% across toddlers to school-age children. A separate age-extension trial in 6–to under-10-year-olds demonstrated immune responses comparable to younger cohorts and favorable safety. Based on these results, Adimmune has submitted to Taiwan’s TFDA an indication-change to extend the eligible vaccination age from under 6 years to under 10 years, aiming to cover elementary-school children. These findings support broader protection against EV71 in the pediatric population.
- On August 17, 2026, GaoDeng Vaccines (stock code 6547) announced at ACPID 2026 in Bandung, Indonesia, that their self-developed Enterovirus 71 (EV-A71) vaccine was invited to deliver an oral presentation. Long-term follow-up shows vaccine-induced neutralizing antibodies persist for at least 6–7 years, with a seroprotection rate of 98.2%. In an immunogenicity and safety trial, children aged 6 to under 10 exhibited immune responses and tolerability comparable to those aged 2 months to under 6 years, with excellent safety in both groups. EV-A71 is a major cause of severe pediatric disease, including encephalitis, myocarditis, and pulmonary edema. The presentation, framed as high-quality and breakthrough, underscores potential durable protection when administered on schedule in early childhood
